posts.title: Notes on Writing for the Web
posts.excerpt: Shorter sentences, clearer headings, and why it matters.
posts.content:
People scan. They do not read. That changes how we write.

Short sentences

One idea per paragraph. One idea per sentence. If a sentence is hard to parse, break it.

Clear headings

Headings are the map. They tell a reader what the section is before they commit to reading it.

Writing for the web is an exercise in respect — respect for the reader's time.

posts.title: The Quiet Power of a Good Title
posts.excerpt: A title is the one element that decides whether a post gets read.
posts.content:
A good title is specific, honest and slightly surprising.

Specific beats vague

"Notes on Writing for the Web" earns more clicks than "Writing Tips".

Honesty beats hype

A title that promises a specific thing and delivers it builds trust. A title that promises everything delivers nothing.

posts.title: Slow Productivity
posts.excerpt: Why deep focus beats constant motion.
posts.content:
Most days I feel productive because I am busy. Busy is not the same as productive.

Deep work

Two hours of uninterrupted focus beats six hours of tab-switching.

The cost of context switching

Every switch costs time to recover. Batch the shallow work and protect the deep work.

The goal is not to be busy all day — it is to finish something meaningful.
